title: Taskified diagnostics and safe-execute sandbox for admin utilities
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Oncall engineers frequently run ad-hoc admin scripts and diagnostic commands from multiple repositories and internal gists. These are brittle, lack structured outputs, and sometimes run with excessive permissions or side effects. We need a way to convert common investigative runbooks into safe, auditable tasks that can run in a sandboxed dry-run mode and, where appropriate, escalate to gated execution with RBAC checks and multi-step confirmations.

Proposal: Implement a 'taskified diagnostics' framework in the admin CLI that: (1) represents runbooks as composable tasks with typed inputs and expected outputs, (2) includes a dry-run sandbox that executes read-only steps against a simulated environment or a replay snapshot, (3) enforces permission checks and an approval gating flow for mutating steps, and (4) emits structured telemetry for every step (duration, tokens scanned, API calls, output hash) and a final provenance record for audit.

Scope: This ticket is focused on the framework, two exemplar runbooks (k8s pod-state forensic and token-cache inspection), and a lightweight sandbox harness that can replay recent traces from observability snapshots. Integrations with the long-term runbook catalog and full UI flows are tracked separately.

Tradeoffs: Building a heavyweight sandbox that fully emulates production is expensive and slow; instead we will start with a read-only replay and a constrained environment shim for mutating commands. The goal is to reduce blast radius while improving reproducibility and auditability.

Links: Drive: https://drive.redwood/company/ops/taskified-diagnostics-spec, PRD: https://confluence.redwood/company/ops/taskified-diagnostics, Prototype CLI repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/admin-task-sandbox, Draft telemetry schema: https://intranet.redwood/telemetry/schemas/admin_diagnostics_v1
acceptance_criteria: Framework accepts YAML-defined tasks with typed inputs and step-level metadata (timeout, read_only flag)
CLI can list available taskified runbooks and show a structured dry-run output without performing mutations
Sandbox replay harness can run two sample runbooks against a recorded observability snapshot and return consistent structured outputs
Permission model enforces that mutating steps require escalation: either a breakglass token OR an approval flow recorded in audit log
Every task run produces a provenance blob (task id, inputs, steps executed, artifacts referenced, operator id, timestamps) stored to internal audit storage
Telemetry emitted for each step includes latency_ms, affected_resources, error_code (if any), and output_digest
design_notes: Prefer declarative task definitions (YAML) to allow non-devs to author runbooks with guardrails
Dry-run mode should substitute writes with a no-op shim that still returns the expected shaped response when possible
Sandbox will reuse existing replay snapshots from observability to avoid maintaining a parallel mock infra
Use existing RBAC bindings and SSO identity — do not invent new auth; map to existing oncall/ops roles
Keep telemetry lightweight; sample verbose outputs for long-running steps to avoid storage blow-up
implementation_plan: Define task YAML schema and validator (week 1)
Build CLI command: admin task run --dry-run/--execute with sandbox toggle (week 2)
Implement sandbox replay harness that pulls a recent observability snapshot and wires read-only shims (week 3)
Add permission checks and approval gating for mutating tasks (week 4)
Instrument telemetry and provenance emission and wire to audit storage (week 5)
Ship two canonical runbooks as examples and doc the authoring guide (week 6)
risk_mitigation: Start with read-only mode to collect developer feedback before enabling mutating tasks
Limit initial rollout to core ops team and a beta group of 3 SREs
Implement automated tests that run the dry-run for each task against a fixture snapshot to detect drift
Require security review for any task that includes a mutating flag before it is allowed in the shared catalog
